description: This line plot illustrates the performance, measured as Micro F1 score in percent, of four different methods—TACRED, TACRED-Revisit, Re-TACRED, and SemEval—across four levels of generated sample sizes (K=8, 16, 32, 64). The x-axis, labeled “Number of Samples Generated,” is categorical and displays discrete values at K=8, K=16, K=32, and K=64. The y-axis, labeled “Micro F1 (%)”, is linear and ranges from 20% to 55%, with major tick marks every 5 percentage points. The TACRED method (blue line with circle markers) starts at approximately 22.5% at K=8, rises to about 28% at K=16, peaks at 30.5% at K=32, and then slightly declines to 29.5% at K=64. The TACRED-Revisit method (orange line with triangle markers) begins at 23% at K=8, increases to 29.5% at K=16, reaches 31% at K=32, and settles at 30% at K=64. The Re-TACRED method (green line with diamond markers) starts at 34.5% at K=8, climbs to 40% at K=16, peaks sharply at 50.5% at K=32, and then drops to 48% at K=64. The SemEval method (red line with square markers) begins at 42% at K=8, steadily increases to 45% at K=16, continues to 47.5% at K=32, and reaches its highest point at 51.5% at K=64. All lines show an overall upward trend, with Re-TACRED and SemEval achieving the highest scores, particularly at K=32 and K=64, respectively.
